one_liner: GPU-resident molecular dynamics engine; on one 6N4O PME benchmark 1.04-2.40x NAMD 3.0b5 and 1.11-1.65x OpenMM 8.1 throughput.
what_it_does: GROMACS is a complete molecular dynamics toolkit, not a drop-in library: gmx grompp turns an .mdp parameter file plus a GROMACS-format topology (.top/.gro) into a run input (.tpr), and gmx mdrun integrates it on CPUs, GPUs, thread-MPI or MPI. Systems parametrized for AMBER or CHARMM must first be expressed as a GROMACS topology (the benchmark ships its own topol.top for the AMBER-built 6N4O system). Programmatic use goes through libgromacs, the gmxapi Python package and the optional NB-LIB nonbonded C++ API under api/.
how_it_is_fast: Short-range forces use the Verlet cut-off scheme with cluster-pair (nbnxm) pair lists, dynamic list pruning and hand-written SIMD kernels (SSE2 through AVX-512, NEON, SVE, VSX) or CUDA/SYCL/HIP/OpenCL kernels. In GPU-resident mode (-update gpu) nonbonded forces, PME (GPU FFT via cuFFT or VkFFT), update and LINCS/SETTLE constraints all run on the GPU, so coordinates and forces stay on the device between neighbour-search steps while the CPU can take bonded forces concurrently. mdrun also auto-tunes at start-up: it raises nstlist with a matching Verlet buffer and, with -tunepme on by default, scales the Coulomb cut-off and PME grid spacing together to balance work while keeping equivalent model physics.
when_to_use: Explicit-solvent biomolecular MD with PME on a single NVIDIA GPU, where the benchmark shows it ahead of both NAMD 3.0b5 (GPU-resident) and OpenMM 8.1 on all 11 GPUs, by at least 1.23x over both on 9 of them (derived from page data), with its largest margins on consumer cards (RTX 4070: 54.0 vs 22.5 and 33.6 ns/day).
Throughput farms of many independent single-GPU runs (equilibration, replicas, free-energy windows) where ns/day per GPU is the cost driver.
Mixed or non-NVIDIA hardware: one code base runs on CUDA, SYCL (Intel GPUs with oneAPI, AMD GPUs with AdaptiveCpp), HIP and OpenCL, plus CPU-only clusters with SIMD kernels.
Multi-GPU or multi-node runs with domain decomposition and GPU PME decomposition (cuFFTMp or HeFFTe builds) when one GPU is not enough.
when_not_to_use: When AMBER pmemd.cuda is an option: in the same suite AMBER 22 is faster than GROMACS on 5 of 11 GPUs (V100 36.89 vs 25.13 ns/day, RTX 3090 43.42 vs 33.03), so GROMACS is not the fastest code on that page.

Workflows that need features the GPU-resident path lacks: per the mdrun docs, GPU update is not supported with mass or constraint free-energy perturbation, virtual sites, Ewald surface correction, replica exchange, constraint pulling, orientation restraints or computational electrophysiology, and LJ-PME and PME orders other than 4 do not run on GPUs; those runs fall back to CPU update and lose much of the advantage.
Custom-force or Python-scripted method development, where OpenMM's API (custom forces, integrators) is the better fit even at lower ns/day.
Embedding MD inside another C++ product under a permissive licence: GROMACS is LGPL-2.1 and its README asks that modified versions be labelled as derived work and not called official GROMACS.
V100-class GPUs, where its lead over NAMD 3.0b5 in this suite shrinks to 1.04x (25.13 vs 24.26 ns/day).

integration.form: built application plus shared/static libgromacs (CMake); gmxapi Python package; optional NB-LIB C++ API install (GMX_INSTALL_NBLIB_API)
integration.dependencies: FFT library (FFTW3 by default, MKL, or bundled slow fftpack; GMX_BUILD_OWN_FFTW can download FFTW); optional CUDA toolkit 12.1+ (main branch), SYCL compiler (oneAPI DPC++ 2024.0+ or AdaptiveCpp 24.02+), ROCm/HIP or OpenCL; optional MPI, cuFFTMp, HeFFTe, VkFFT
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; on the current main branch GCC 11+, Clang 14+ or MSVC 2019, CMake 3.28+; CUDA 12.1+ and compute capability 5.0+ for CUDA builds (older releases such as the benchmarked 2023.3 had lower minimums, not checked)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS and Windows; x86-64 (SSE2, SSE4.1, AVX, AVX2, AVX-512), AArch64 (NEON, SVE), POWER (VSX); GPUs: NVIDIA (CUDA), AMD (SYCL/AdaptiveCpp or HIP), Intel (SYCL/oneAPI), Apple M-series (OpenCL)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented for library use; mdrun parallelizes internally with OpenMP threads, thread-MPI ranks or MPI.

gotchas: Harness flaw that understates GROMACS rather than inflating it: the NgFEP script runs only 10,000 steps (10 ps) without -resethway or -resetstep, so the reported ns/day includes start-up and the PME tuning phase that the mdrun docs say these options exist to exclude; it also forces -bonded cpu with -update gpu and keeps nstenergy/nstlog at 100 and tau_t 0.1 ps, while the mdrun docs warn that frequent energy computation and coupling carry large overhead in GPU-resident runs. NAMD and OpenMM ran 100,000 steps. This fits the gap to MDBench (GROMACS 2023.2 at 88.4 ns/day on an A100 for 6n4o, snippet only, against 59.5 here).

The 'fixed 144^3 PME grid, 0.8 nm cut-off' in the workload is not guaranteed for GROMACS: pmeTuningIsSupported() in src/gromacs/ewald/pme_load_balancing.cpp enables the default -tunepme whenever nonbondeds run on a GPU, so mdrun may have run a larger Coulomb cut-off with a coarser grid (equivalent accuracy, but not the same grid NAMD and AMBER used).

Rankings flip with versions and run settings: an MDBench snippet shows NAMD 3.0b3 at 42.06 ns/day against GROMACS 2021.4 at 29.5 ns/day on the same A100 for 6n4o, the reverse of this suite, so treat the 1.5x A100 lead as specific to GROMACS 2023 GPU-resident runs.

Builds are tied to one SIMD level chosen at configure time (GMX_SIMD, default AUTO detects the build host), so a binary built on a newer node can fail or run slowly elsewhere; the known-issues page also lists a severe SVE slowdown with LLVM 20 and test failures with GCC 12-14 on POWER9.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other molecular dynamics engine is catalogued in geometry-spatial; the spatial-index siblings (nanoflann, ArborX, Pkd-tree) are libraries for neighbour queries you embed, whereas GROMACS's cell and pair lists are internal to mdrun, so pick it when you need whole MD simulations rather than a reusable neighbour-search structure.
verified_claims_summary: An independent lab suite (NgFEP/NgFEP-assessment) ran the 6N4O Argonaute2/miR-122 system (AMBER-parametrized, PME, 0.8 nm cut-off, 1 fs, NPT) five times per GPU with GROMACS 2023.3 (-nb gpu -pme gpu -update gpu -bonded cpu, 4 OpenMP threads), NAMD 3.0b5 multicore-CUDA in GPU-resident mode and OpenMM 8.1 CUDA mixed precision; per-GPU means recomputed this session from all 48 .dat files the plotting notebook reads match the record (A100 59.47 vs 39.19 vs 36.00 ns/day; 1.04-2.40x NAMD and 1.11-1.65x OpenMM over 11 GPUs, derived from page data). Builds, compilers, CUDA and driver versions and host CPUs are not stated, and thermostats, barostats and run lengths differ between codes.
status_note: Actively developed (GitHub read-only mirror of gitlab.com/gromacs/gromacs, 24,268 commits, last commit 2026-10-06), LGPL-2.1 and packaged widely; usable as an application today, but library reuse is limited to libgromacs, gmxapi and the opt-in NB-LIB API.
